title: Mathematics for modelling and inference · Rung 1
subtitle: Reading the equations in a paper instead of skipping them
coverLine: Rates, totals, tables of numbers, chance, and where a system settles
subject: S02
author: Dr. Harsh Maheshwari

about.why: Most papers on body weight carry a few equations, and most readers skip them. The argument is often in those lines. Book 0 named the derivative and the integral and asked you to work out neither. This book asks you to work them out, on body stores rather than on made-up curves. It adds the few tools that the equations in these papers keep using: tables of numbers multiplied together, the arithmetic of chance, and the point where a changing system stops changing.
about.howToRead: Read Book 0 and Book 1 first, or at least the sections this book names as it goes. Then read this one in order: each section assumes everything before it. Do the practice problems in each section before you read on, with a pen and a calculator. Keep a notebook open as you go. By the end it should hold ten equations from papers you have read, each written out in words. What this book does not teach yet: the product and chain rules, partial derivatives, likelihood, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, regression and causal inference. Later books in the series take them up; “inference” in the title is where this subject’s rungs are heading.

blurb: A short book of mathematics for reading research on obesity. It covers the rate of change and the running total worked out rather than named, the number e, a table of numbers and what multiplying by one does, a random quantity with its average and spread, and the point where a changing quantity settles. Then it shows how to read an equation symbol by symbol, and how to follow a derivation line by line without jumping to the result.

sections.title: Reading the symbols in a methods section
The derivative: the rate at an instant, computed
The few rules that do the differentiating
The number e, natural logarithms and change proportional to amount
The integral of a rate is the change in the stock
Undoing a derivative: antiderivatives and the fundamental theorem
A differential equation: a rule that gives the rate from the state
Equilibrium: where the rate is zero
Highest and lowest points: slope zero and curvature
Vectors as data rows, and the weighted sum
A matrix, and what multiplying by one does
A column that is a weighted sum of other columns
A random variable and its distribution
Variance, and why independent errors add as squares
Four kinds of equation, and the notebook entry
